comment: The tape's width is fixed when recording starts and does not change afterwards, so repatching the input later cannot split a stereo loop. A pristine copy of the first recording is kept off the tape and splice restores it and puts the age back to zero. The age jack steps once per full turn of the tape regardless of overlap, while eoc and ramp follow the heard repeat, which with overlap up is more often. The two gate jacks and the record and overdub buttons are levels rather than edges. The panel prints tabes, decay, wow, overlap, send, cv four times, dub lvl, rec, dub, splice, in, gate, gate, trig, send, return, age, ramp, eoc and out.
